title: CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed

paragraphs.en: Anne found it difficult to return to her usual routine after the excitement of the concert. She felt that life could never be the same as before those faraway days. Initially, she told Diana that she might not adjust easily.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在音乐会的兴奋过后很难恢复到往常的生活节奏。她觉得自己的生活再也无法回到那些遥远日子之前的状态。最初，她告诉戴安娜自己可能需要一段时间才能适应过来。

paragraphs.en: "I'm sure, Diana, that concerts change people," Anne said mournfully. "Marilla is sensible, but I don't think I'd want to be sensible because they are so unromantic."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜，我敢肯定音乐会能改变人，”安妮悲伤地说，“玛丽拉很理智，但我可不想因为它们太缺乏浪漫而变得理智。”

paragraphs.en: Despite her reservations, Avonlea school gradually returned to its usual activities. The concert left some lingering effects. Ruby Gillis and Emma White, who had quarreled over seating, no longer sat together.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管安妮有些顾虑，埃文利学校渐渐恢复了往日的活力。那场音乐会留下了一些余波，之前因为座位争执而闹翻的鲁比·吉尔思和艾玛·怀特也不再坐在一起了。

paragraphs.en: Josie Pye and Julia Bell avoided each other for three months after Josie told Bessie Wright about Julia's recitation bow. The Sloanes and the Bells also stopped interacting due to a dispute over their roles in the program.
paragraphs.zh: 乔西·皮和朱莉娅·贝尔在乔西向贝丝·赖特透露了朱莉娅的朗诵礼节后，整整三个月相互避而不见。斯洛恩一家和贝尔一家也因节目中的角色争执而停止了往来。

paragraphs.en: Finally, Charlie Sloane fought Moody Spurgeon MacPherson because of Moody Spurgeon’s comment on Anne's recitations. Ella May, Moody Spurgeon's sister, refused to speak to Anne for the rest of winter. These minor conflicts aside, Miss Stacy's class continued smoothly and regularly.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，查理·斯洛恩与莫迪·斯戈伦·麦菲森因为后者对安妮朗读的评价而起了争执。莫迪·斯戈伦的妹妹埃拉·梅因此整个冬天都不愿与安妮说话。除了这些小摩擦外，史蒂西小姐的班级依旧顺利且规律地进行着。

paragraphs.en: Winter passed quietly, with little snow, allowing Anne and Diana to walk the Birch Path almost daily. On Anne’s thirteenth birthday, they chatted merrily along this path, eager to observe nature for their upcoming composition on "A Winter's Walk in the Woods."
paragraphs.zh: 冬天悄然而过，雪量不大，这让安妮和戴安娜几乎每天都能漫步在白桦林小径上。到了安妮十三岁生日那天，两人边走边聊，兴致勃勃地观察着周围的自然景色，为她们即将进行的“冬日森林散步”作文做准备。

paragraphs.en: "Can you believe I'm thirteen today?" Anne said, her voice filled with wonder. "It feels like a new chapter of life has begun.
paragraphs.zh: “你能相信今天我正好十三岁吗？”安妮的声音里充满了惊奇，“感觉就像是人生的新篇章刚刚开启。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Stacy reminded us we need to be observant for our assignment. Two more years until I’m truly grown up—quite exciting!"
paragraphs.zh: 斯蒂西太太提醒我们，要留意观察以完成任务。还有两年我才算是真正长大——真是令人兴奋！

paragraphs.en: Diana mentioned Ruby Gillis’s plans to have a beau at fifteen. "Ruby thinks only about boys," Anne replied, her tone disapproving. "She acts so indifferent when people write her name in notices, but she's secretly pleased."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜提到鲁比·吉尔思打算十五岁就有男朋友了。“鲁比只想着男孩的事，”安妮回答道，语气中带着不赞成，“她明明在公告里看到自己的名字时表现得很不在意，但实际上心里却很高兴。”

paragraphs.en: Anne reflected on her own behavior, trying to emulate Mrs. Allan, whom she admired greatly. "I often say unkind things without thinking," she admitted. "Mrs. Lynde says ministers shouldn't be so attached to mortals, yet everyone has flaws.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮反思自己的行为，努力效仿她非常敬佩的阿兰太太。“我常常不经思考就说些不中听的话，”她承认道，“雷切尔·林德说牧师不应该过于牵挂凡人，但每个人都有缺点。”

paragraphs.en: I had a talk with Mrs. Allan about besetting sins last Sunday."
paragraphs.zh: 我上个星期天和艾伦太太谈了谈经常犯的罪过。

paragraphs.en: Diana added, "In four years, we can put our hair up." She noted Alice Bell’s hairstyle but dismissed it as ridiculous. "I'll wait until seventeen," Diana concluded.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜补充道：“四年后，我们可以把头发扎起来。”她注意到艾丽丝·贝尓的发型，但觉得那未免太离奇了。“我等到十七岁再考虑这件事吧。”戴安娜最后说道。

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed, "If I had Alice Bell's crooked nose, I wouldn't say anything unkind. But comparing it with mine is vanity." She continued, "I've been thinking too much about my nose since that compliment years ago."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，“要是我有艾丽丝·贝尔回弯的鼻子，我绝不会说出那些不中听的话。但与我的鼻子相比，这未免太自作多情了。”她接着说：“自从那句恭维话以来，我一直都在过多地思考我的鼻子。”

paragraphs.en: Diana replied, "I won’t mind writing the woods composition when it comes. The one due Monday seems impossible. Miss Stacy telling us to write a story from our imagination?"
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜回答说：“我不介意等到写森林题材的文章。周一那篇似乎根本不可能完成，斯泰西小姐让我们根据想象编写一篇故事？”

paragraphs.en: Anne retorted, "It's as easy as blinking." Diana countered, "Easy for you with your imagination, but what if you were born without one? Do you have your composition done?"
paragraphs.zh: 安妮反驳说：“这就像眨眼一样简单。”戴安娜回应道：“对你这样富有想象力的人来说或许容易，但如果你生来就没有想象力呢？你的作文写好了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Anne nodded, her face betraying a hint of pride she tried to suppress. "I wrote it last Monday evening. It’s called 'The Jealous Rival; or In Death Not Divided.'
paragraphs.zh: 安妮点了点头，脸上流露出一丝她试图抑制的自豪之情。“我上周一晚上写的。题目叫《嫉妒的对手；或在死亡中不分你我》。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla said it was nonsense, but Matthew thought it was fine."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉说这纯粹是胡说八道，但马修却觉得挺好的。

paragraphs.en: Diana showed interest, asking, "What happened to Cordelia and Geraldine?"
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜表现出兴趣，问道：“科黛莉亚和杰拉尔丁发生了什么事？”

paragraphs.en: Bertram DeVere came to the village where Geraldine lived and fell in love with her. He saved her when her horse-drawn carriage crashed, carrying her home three miles. Geraldine accepted Bertram's proposal with a long speech, and he gifted her a diamond ring and ruby necklace.
paragraphs.zh: 伯特兰·德弗雷来到盖丽琳所在的村庄，一见钟情。当盖丽琳乘坐马车翻车受伤时，他及时赶到，将她救出，并护送她回家三英里远。盖丽琳用一番长篇大论接受了伯特兰的求婚，作为礼物，他还送给盖丽琳一枚钻石戒指和一条红宝石项链。

paragraphs.en: Despite their engagement, Cordelia secretly loved Bertram too. When she saw the gifts, she became jealous and vowed to prevent their marriage.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管柯黛丽亚已经订婚，她内心深处仍然爱着伯特兰。看到那些礼物时，她不禁生起嫉妒之心，并暗自发誓要阻止他们成婚。

paragraphs.en: One evening, on a bridge over a rushing stream, Cordelia pushed Geraldine into the water in a fit of rage. Bertram tried to save her but couldn't swim and they both drowned. Their bodies were found later, buried together with an imposing funeral.
paragraphs.zh: 一天傍晚，在一条湍急溪流上的小桥上，科黛丽亚因一时气愤将杰拉丁德推入水中。伯特兰试图救她，但他不会游泳，最终两人一同溺亡。他们的遗体后来被发现，合葬在一起，并举行了庄重的葬礼。

paragraphs.en: Cordelia's guilt drove her insane, leading her to be institutionalized.
paragraphs.zh: 科黛丽亚的内疚让她精神失常，最终被送进了精神病院。

paragraphs.en: Diana sighed, admiring Anne's creativity. "How can you come up with such thrilling stories in your head, Anne? I wish my imagination was as good."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜叹了口气，羡慕地看着安妮。“你怎么能在脑子里想出如此惊心动魄的故事呢，安妮？我希望我的想象力也能这么好。”

paragraphs.en: Anne replied cheerfully, "You just need to develop it. I've got a plan. Let's start a story club and write for practice.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮愉快地回答：“你只需要把它发展起来。我已经有了一个计划，咱们可以成立一个故事俱乐部，边写边练。”

paragraphs.en: You'll get better with time. Miss Stacy says cultivating the imagination is important."
paragraphs.zh: 你会随着时间的推移变得更好的，斯泰西小姐说培养想象力很重要。

paragraphs.en: The story club began with Diana and Anne. Soon Jane Andrews and Ruby Gillis joined, along with others who wanted to improve their imaginations. Boys were not allowed.
paragraphs.zh: 故事俱乐部最初由戴安娜和安妮发起。很快，简·安德鲁斯和ruby·吉尔思也加入了进来，还有一些希望提升想象力的其他女孩。男孩们被禁止参加。

paragraphs.en: Each member had to submit one story a week. They read aloud and discussed each other's work. Anne wrote under the pen name Rosamond Montmorency.
paragraphs.zh: 每位成员每周必须提交一个故事，他们轮流朗读并讨论彼此的作品。安妮用笔名罗莎蒙德·蒙莫兰西写作。

paragraphs.en: The girls produced stories of varying quality—Ruby was overly sentimental, Jane's were sensible, and Diana included too many murders.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们提交的故事质量参差不齐—— Ruby 的故事过于感伤，Jane 的则颇为现实，而戴安娜的作品中却出现了太多凶杀情节。

paragraphs.en: Anne told Marilla that it was interesting. "We keep all our stories sacredly for future generations to read. We use pseudonyms.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮告诉玛丽拉这很有趣。“我们把这些故事都精心保存下来，留待后人阅读。为了保密起见，我们都用了笔名。”

paragraphs.en: Ruby writes too much romance, while Jane avoids love scenes. I often suggest topics since I have countless ideas."
paragraphs.zh: 鲁比写的爱情小说过多，而简则避开爱的场景。我经常提出话题，因为我脑子里有很多好点子。

paragraphs.en: Marilla scoffed, "This story-writing is the most foolish idea yet. You'll fill your heads with nonsense and waste time on lessons instead of reading stories."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉嗤之以鼻，“这写故事的主意真是荒唐至极。你们只会胡思乱想，耽误了上课的时间反而去读那些故事。”

paragraphs.en: Anne explained to Marilla that they always included morals in their stories. "We reward the good and punish the bad," she said. "Mr. Allan and his wife agreed the morals were excellent, though they laughed at wrong moments."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮向玛丽拉解释说，她们的故事总是包含道德教育。“我们褒奖善行，惩罚恶行。”她说，“艾伦先生和他的妻子认为我们的道德观念很好，尽管他们有时笑错了时候。”

paragraphs.en: Anne preferred it when people cried during the sad parts of her stories.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮更喜欢人们在她故事的悲伤部分流眼泪。

paragraphs.en: Jane and Ruby often shed tears when Anne reached the emotional sections. Diana had written to Aunt Josephine about their club, and Aunt Josephine responded that they should send some stories. They selected four best pieces and mailed them to Miss Barry.
paragraphs.zh: 简和鲁比常常在安妮讲到情感充沛的部分时流下眼泪。戴安娜曾给乔治安娜阿姨写信提到她们的故事俱乐部，乔治安娜阿姨回信说应该寄一些故事过来。于是她们挑选了四篇最好的作品寄给了巴里小姐。

paragraphs.en: To their surprise, she found them highly amusing despite their tragic nature and numerous deaths.
paragraphs.zh: 令她惊讶的是，尽管这些故事充满了悲剧色彩并且涉及众多死亡场景，她们依然觉得非常有趣。

paragraphs.en: Marilla replied, "I wouldn't say there's much hope." She added, "Mrs. Allan was never as silly or forgetful as you are." Anne hoped she could become more like Mrs. Allan when she grew up.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“我可不会抱太大希望。”她又补充道：“阿兰太太从不像你这么傻或健忘。”安妮希望自己长大后能变得像阿兰太太那样。

paragraphs.en: Anne replied seriously, "No; but she wasn't always so good as she is now either." She continued, "She told me that when she was a girl, she used to get into scrapes and was a dreadful mischief. Hearing this made me feel encouraged.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮认真地说：“不是的，但她也不是一直像现在这么好的。”她继续说道：“她告诉我，小时候她经常闯祸，是个十足的捣蛋鬼。听到这些，我感到备受鼓舞。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla, do I seem wicked for feeling encouraged because others were bad? Mrs. Lynde says it is. She gets shocked whenever anyone admits to being naughty, no matter how small they are."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉，我是不是显得有些邪恶，因为别人做了坏事而感到庆幸？雷切尔·林德夫人这么说。她只要有人承认自己淘气过，不论对方多小，都会大吃一惊。

paragraphs.en: Marilla responded, "The way I see it now, Anne, is that you should get those dishes washed. You've spent half an hour chatting instead of working. Learn to work first and talk later."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“依我看，安妮，你现在应该把那些盘子洗了。你已经花了半个多小时聊天而没有干活。先学会工作再说话吧。”
